correctness.rationale: The direct pair-distance formula for disjoint weight-two supports is 8 minus cycle-induced edges. Disjoint support gives the universal n/2 upper bound; a second incidence bound excludes length-seven/eight size-three and length-nine size-four. Constructive Euler tours of connected circulant 4-regular graphs attain all n>=10 and zero insertion preserves pair-distance for odd n. Every even equality case partitions coordinates and forces a simple 4-regular Euler graph. At n=10 this is K5; exact DP gives 528 starting-0 tours, 22 unlabeled-support codes, and an independently exhaustive direct 45-vertex compatibility-graph search yields 22 and D10 orbits 2,10,10. Both packaged verifiers were run successfully. No finite check stands in for the general proof.

originality.rationale: The core new comparison-resistant assertion is the converse characterization of every optimal even full-support weight-two binary code by a 4-regular simple Euler circuit and, at the natural first full-support length ten, the exact 22 labeled-coordinate code sets and 3 dihedral orbits. Chee et al. 2012 provides the Eulerian construction technique but does not count or characterize all weight-two equalities. Elishco et al. treat constant pair weight four at pair-distance eight rather than the present seven. Zhao–Chang treat pair-weight four distance seven but were not readable beyond the abstract/preview: broad size claims may be prior; this is not a priority claim for numerical bounds. No inspected source or indexed mathematical record entails the exact equality census, subject to residual full-text risk.
residual_risks: The full 2025 Zhao–Chang paper is unavailable and might contain equality-case statements that were not in its abstract; its optimal-size conclusions may subsume part of the size theorem.
Searches of indexed literature and record summaries do not establish bibliographic uniqueness; unindexed Euler-tour classifications may overlap.
A future or inaccessible exhaustive classification could imply the 22 / three-orbit count.

value.rationale: The first full-support extremal blocklength n=10 of the binary weight-two cyclic distance-seven problem is a canonical non-arbitrary equality case. The finding gives a full all-length exact size spectrum and structural equality theorem for every even n>=10, then classifies all first-threshold optima (22 into three natural symmetry classes). This determines design diversity at the onset of sharpness and identifies a rigorous graph-theoretic invariant for further finite enumeration. Known Euler existence and bounds alone do not supply this complete classification; neither improved general-code bounds nor higher-weight results are asserted.
